arguments.value: Harold Brent McKnight (1952–2004) was a United States District Judge for the Western District of North Carolina, appointed by President George W. Bush in 2003 and serving until his death later that year. Born in Mooresville, North Carolina, he earned a B.A. from the University of North Carolina, an M.A. from the University of Oxford’s Magdalen College, and a J.D. from the University of North Carolina School of Law. Before joining the federal bench, McKnight served as a U.S. Magistrate Judge for the Western District of North Carolina from 1993 to 2003, as an assistant district attorney for North Carolina from 1982 to 1988, and as a judge on the North Carolina District Court for the Twenty-Sixth Judicial District from 1989 to 1993. He also taught as a visiting lecturer at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte and as an adjunct assistant professor at Wingate University.
